output.summary: Checkpoint rules (latest-per-head, fork-point chain in this history, nearest, stale skip), whole-branch blockers for incremental pr-ready, token recorded, docs; merge-from-main widening documented (#182).

findings.issue: The checkpoint's fork point and pr-ready's whole-branch blocker scope come from gitcontext.DefaultBase, which falls back to HEAD~1 with no local main/master (develop/trunk repos, CI checkouts).
findings.consequence: Reproduced in a develop-trunk repo: incremental pr-ready passes (exit 0) with an open task-done blocker on a file changed before the checkpoint; a narrow-base marker becomes the checkpoint.

findings.issue: Only a later marker at the same head withdraws a checkpoint; a later NEEDS_REVISION at a descendant head whose base is at/before the checkpoint also judged the checkpoint's code but is ignored.
findings.consequence: Reproduced: PASS@C1 (base main), NEEDS_REVISION@C2 (base main), C3 -> checkpoint C1, incremental pr-ready C1..C3 passes, hiding the rejection.

findings.issue: The emulated advisory comes only from the marker at the current base..HEAD; a checkpoint chain resting on in-session-emulated markers is never surfaced (also taskdone, epicready).
findings.consequence: A self-attested checkpoint plus a subagent-adjudicated increment yields a clean whole-branch PASS with no adversarial-review-emulated advisory.

findings.issue: Fork-point wiring is untested against real git: DefaultBase->HEAD~1 and forkPoint := head mutants survive; no CLI test refuses a narrow-base marker.
findings.consequence: A fork-point regression would accept narrow-base checkpoints silently.

findings.issue: The cycle guard is untested; the only real cycle is a base==head marker (record-lenses --base HEAD), where vouches(h) recurses into itself.
findings.consequence: Removing the guard makes checkpoint resolution overflow the stack on such a marker with the suite green.

findings.issue: The exit-2 message and commands/skills docs say 'no passing review recorded' / 'with none recorded', but since 7ac29ab it also exits 2 when passing reviews exist but none qualifies (superseded, narrow base, no base, rebased chain); commands/review-pr-ready.md lacks the whole-branch-blockers sentence.
findings.consequence: Users who just recorded a narrow-base review are told none exists.

findings.issue: The CLI Incremental wiring for task-done and epic-ready is untested (deleting either survives).
findings.consequence: Incremental task-done/epic-ready runs could silently record the SHA instead of last-reviewed.
